title: Capital Is Rotating Fast — Here's Where the Money Lands Today
subTitle:
$487 million in 24-hour volume just flooded through Ethereum. Over on SOL, another $251 million piled in with a 4.41% daily gain. Meanwhile, three small-caps — M, RIF, GWEI — posted 68%, 45%, and 21% moves respectively. Capital is not sitting still right now. It is sprinting across the majors and bleeding into micro-caps at a pace that tells you one thing clearly: risk appetite is waking up.

Let me break down where it is going, what the charts say, and what to watch next.

Ethereum leads the rotation

ETH printed $1,623.17 on Binance as of this morning, up 2.59% in 24 hours. The market cap sits at $195.40 billion according to CoinMarketCap — still the second-largest asset in the space by a wide margin, and still the place where institutional and smart money tends to rotate first when sentiment shifts.

The chart structure tells a clean story. Over the past 72 hours, buyers have been defending $1,550.20 as support. That level held multiple times this week, each bounce getting a little stronger. On the upside, $1,646.26 is the resistance ceiling that has capped every rally attempt.

Right now, ETH is trading just below that resistance — close enough that a clean break above $1,646.26 on solid volume would flip it into a new support base and open up room for momentum to accelerate. If it fails to break through and gets rejected here, the natural pullback target is that $1,550.20 floor where buyers have already shown they are willing to step in.

The setup is straightforward. If ETH holds above $1,550.20 on any dip, the dip-buy thesis stays intact — buyers are in control of the range. If it loses $1,550.20 on a closing basis, the structure shifts bearish and sellers take the wheel. That is the line in the sand.

Want to position around that range? Tap $ETH to open the chart and track both levels in real time.

Solana outperforming on momentum

SOL is the louder story today. $78.60 on Binance with a 4.41% gain — nearly double ETH's move on a percentage basis. The market cap reached $45.47 billion per CoinMarketCap, and the 24-hour volume of $251.16 million signals real conviction behind the push, not just thin-book wicks.

The 72h chart shows support sitting at $71.90 — a level that has acted as the launchpad for this current leg up. Resistance is pinned at $78.96, which means SOL is literally knocking on the door right now. Trading at $78.60 with resistance at $78.96 is as close to a decision point as a chart can get.

If SOL clears $78.96 with volume confirmation, that breakout becomes the trade of the week — the kind of move where momentum chases momentum. If it gets rejected here and slides back, the first level buyers need to hold is $71.90. Lose that, and the bullish structure from this week unwinds fast.

Tap $SOL to watch that $78.96 level live. A break above it is the kind of signal that does not come around every day.

The small-cap signal

Here is what makes today interesting beyond the majors. M surged 68.5%, RIF jumped 45.9%, and GWEI added 21.1% — all in 24 hours per CoinMarketCap. When alt-laggers start printing moves like this while ETH and SOL are trending up, it is the classic sign of capital cascading down the risk curve. Money enters through BTC and ETH, then rotates into L1s like SOL, and then trickles into micro-caps. We are watching that rotation play out in real time.

The macro backdrop adds fuel. Metaplanet just added 2,823 BTC to its treasury, pushing total holdings past 43,000 Bitcoin — corporate accumulation at scale. Robinhood is linking with dYdX Labs to launch a new DEX called Arcus, bridging retail flow into decentralized derivatives. And OpenAI is reportedly weighing a 5% stake deal with the US government, per the Financial Times — a reminder that the lines between AI, policy, and crypto capital flows are blurring fast.

What this means for your next move

The rotation map is clear. Capital flows from Bitcoin stability into ETH's $195 billion market cap, then accelerates into SOL's faster-moving chart, and finally spills into small-caps that amplify the momentum. ETH at $1,623.17 and SOL at $78.60 are both sitting just below their respective resistance ceilings. Both have well-defined support floors. Both offer traders a clean if-then framework: hold support and the trend continues, lose it and the thesis resets.

Not financial advice.

What is your read — are we seeing the start of a sustained rotation, or is this a short squeeze before the next leg down? Drop your take below.

Stay sharp, stay liquid.

The main question of a trending trade isn’t “where to enter,” but “where I made a mistake.” 🧭

I determine invalidation BEFORE entering. If I can’t name the level at which the idea is dead—there is no trade. Period.

For a trend long, it’s usually the last meaningful low of the structure. Price closes below it—then the sequence of rising lows is broken, the trend is in question, and I’m out. No “I’ll wait for it to bounce back.”

This is risk management: the stop is logically tied to the structure, not to an arbitrary percentage of your account. From the invalidation level, I calculate R:R and the position size.

For $ETH  I keep it simple: above the demand zone—priority goes to trend longs; closing below it—priority shifts, and I stop buying dips.

The market owes you nothing. Your job is to know in advance when you’re wrong.

On-chain monitoring shows that Machi continued to sell three Bored Apes today. The total deal price was 27.42 ETH, about $440,000, which is roughly a loss of 25 ETH compared with its cost basis. Market interpretation suggests that this move is mainly to raise additional margin and continue adding to its Ethereum long exposure. This development reflects that high-net-worth players remain somewhat optimistic about ETH’s outlook, but the high-leverage strategy also means volatility risk still needs to be closely watched.

2. Wang Chun’s large ETH and WBTC deposits/withdrawals draw attention
On-chain data indicates that Wang Chun, founder of F2Pool, recently deposited 16,842 ETH and 60 WBTC to Binance, with a total value of over $30 million. Meanwhile, in recent activity, he cumulatively withdrew 91,945 ETH and 973 WBTC from Binance, bringing the overall scale close to $220 million. Large deposits/withdrawals are often viewed by the market as an important signal of fund reallocation, risk management, or asset allocation adjustments. With large on-chain movements in both ETH and WBTC occurring simultaneously, it also suggests that the chips of major assets are still actively circulating; future developments are worth monitoring.

3. Meta’s plan to sell idle AI computing power sparks market debate
The news that Meta plans to sell its idle AI computing capacity externally triggered a strong reaction from capital markets, and the company’s stock jumped 9% in a single day. Reports say Meta’s current infrastructure utilization rate is about 65%, with roughly 35% of capacity still available for monetization. The optimistic view is that this move can help improve cash flow and increase the efficiency of returns on massive capital expenditures; the cautious view worries that it may be interpreted as a shift in the pace of its frontier AI investment. If the plan proceeds, Meta may directly enter the cloud computing supply track, creating competitive pressure for existing AI infrastructure companies.

4. Samsung Electronics’ 2x Long Southbound ETF in Hong Kong plunges sharply intraday
In the Hong Kong market, Samsung Electronics’ 2x Long Southbound ETF fell more than 25% at one point during the afternoon trading session, significantly amplifying short-term volatility. A 2x leveraged ETF itself has high convexity; when the underlying price swings sharply, market sentiment weakens, or leverage rebalancing effects come into play, it often results in unexpectedly large upside or downside moves. This anomaly once again reminds the market that leveraged ETFs are generally better suited for short-term trading and investors with a higher risk tolerance. In the current volatile environment, controlling position size and liquidity risk is especially important.

5. Japan’s Ministry of Finance stays silent on yen fluctuations
Regarding the yen’s sudden rise earlier, Japan’s Ministry of Finance refused to comment in its latest statement. Although the official side did not release more information, FX markets typically treat such silence as an important signal to assess policy stance. For the crypto market, yen volatility often interacts with global risk-off sentiment, the strength of the U.S. dollar, and expectations for macro liquidity. If exchange-rate fluctuations continue to intensify, it may further affect the pricing of risk assets in Asian trading hours, including the short-term sentiment toward major crypto assets such as BTC and ETH.

title: Altcoin Season Whispers as $BTC and $ETH Test Critical Levels
subTitle:
Capital is starting to move. After weeks of Bitcoin dominance holding the spotlight, the last 24 hours have quietly signaled something that long-term observers recognize immediately: the rotation wheel is beginning to turn.

According to CoinMarketCap, Bitcoin sits at $60,291.40 on Binance, up 2.65% over the past 24 hours with $1.43 billion in trading volume and a market cap of $1.208 trillion. Ethereum mirrors that same 2.65% daily move, trading at $1,618.55 with $487.70 million in volume and a $195.34 billion market cap. That symmetry is not a coincidence. When $ETH matches $BTC stride for stride, capital is not exiting crypto — it is redistributing within it.

And the real evidence of rotation is not in the majors at all. It is in the names most traders scrolled past this morning. M token surged 67.3%. RIF climbed 41.8%. SYN added 20.3%. These are not random pumps on low-liquidity pairs. They are signals that risk appetite is expanding beyond the safety of Bitcoin and into the broader altcoin complex. Historically, this is the phase that precedes either a broad rally or a sharp mean-reversion. The difference between the two outcomes usually comes down to whether the majors hold their structural support.

That is where today's chart levels matter more than any headline.

Bitcoin's 72h support sits at $57,800.19 and resistance caps it at $61,334.00. The current price of $60,291.40 places $BTC in the upper half of that range, pressing toward resistance. If Bitcoin holds above the $57,800 support zone on any pullback, the structure remains bullish and rotation into altcoins can continue with conviction. If it loses that level on a daily close, the risk-off cascade that analysts have been warning about — and one Cointelegraph headline today underscores — could accelerate, pulling the entire market lower and punishing the altcoins that just rallied hardest.

Ethereum tells a similar story with tighter boundaries. Support at $1,550.20 and resistance at $1,646.26 give $ETH a defined corridor. At $1,618.55, it is sitting just below resistance. A clean break above $1,646.26 would be a significant technical signal, not just for Ethereum but for every token that trades against it on decentralized exchanges. Conversely, if $ETH fails to hold $1,550.20, the rotation narrative weakens fast because Ethereum is the liquidity backbone of the altcoin ecosystem. Tap $ETH to trade that level if you are watching the breakout setup.

The macro backdrop adds layers of complexity. France is escalating its response to a wave of crypto-related physical attacks now totaling 77 incidents — a grim reminder that as adoption grows, so do the vectors of risk that have nothing to do with price charts. Meanwhile, Robinhood linking with dYdX Labs to launch a new DEX called Arcus represents the kind of institutional infrastructure build that compounds over years, not days. These developments rarely move markets overnight, but they shape the terrain that the next cycle will be built on.

One analyst warning making the rounds today suggests Bitcoin could drop further after its worst June performance since 2022. That is a data point worth respecting, but not one worth fearing in isolation. #Just entered the crypto world? Newbies, remember these three things—they can help you avoid a lot of detours:

First: Don’t think about getting rich quick—learn to stay alive

The crypto market isn’t an ATM. What you earn is money from emotional swings, not a passive “set-and-forget” machine that just keeps paying.
When it pumps, it gets crazy. When it dumps, it gets even crazier.
What new traders should train isn’t just reading charts—it’s controlling your impulses—
Never be fully invested, never go all-in.
Don’t bet next month’s rent or next year’s car loan on a single judgment.

Second: Only trade what you understand—don’t touch what you don’t

“This coin can do 100x,” “friend’s insider info,” “the group admin calls the shots”—
Just listen and move on.
If you can’t understand a project, not touching it is the best risk control.
Major coins may rise more slowly, but when they fall, at least they give you time to react.
For beginners, stability matters ten thousand times more than excitement.

Third: Make money with the market; lose money—all on yourself

Most people don’t lose to the market—they lose to themselves:
They chase after a little pump, cut after a little dip. Once emotions kick in, they enter contracts chaotically and add position size randomly.
The real fundamentals you should practice are just three:
Follow the trend—don’t guess tops and bottoms;
DCA in batches—don’t go in with a single All In;
Keep your emotions steady—it's more useful than “technical skills.”

The crypto world isn’t a race to see who runs fastest—it’s about who survives the longest.

---

#刚进币圈的新手，记住这三条，能帮你少走很多弯路：

第一条：别想着暴富，先学会活着

币圈不是提款机，赚的是情绪波动的钱，不是躺赚的永动机。
涨起来疯，跌起来更疯。
新手最该练的，不是看K线，是管住手——
永远不满仓，永远不梭哈。
别把下个月的房租、明年的车贷，压在一次判断上。

第二条：只玩看得懂的，别碰听不懂的

“这币要百倍”“朋友内幕”“群主喊单”——
这些话听听就好。
看不懂的项目，不碰就是最好的风控。
主流币涨得慢，但跌起来至少给你反应时间。
对新手来说，稳，比刺激重要一万倍。

第三条：赚钱靠行情，亏钱全怪自己

大多数人不是输给市场，是输给自己：
涨一点就追，跌一点就割，情绪一上来，合约乱开，仓位乱加。
真正该练的基本功就三样：
看趋势，别猜顶底；
分批定投，别一把All in；
情绪稳住，比技术管用。

币圈不是比谁跑得快，是比谁活得久。

---

subTitle:
Ethereum sits at $1,616.84 on Binance right now, just 1.8% below its 72-hour resistance of $1,646.26 and roughly 4.3% above its 72-hour support at $1,550.20. That is a tight range, and tight ranges tend to resolve with conviction. The question every disciplined trader should be asking is not which direction it breaks — it is whether they are positioned to survive both outcomes.

Let us start with the ETH versus BTC relationship, because that is where the real signal lives. $BTC is trading at $60,204.60, up 2.38% on the day with a 24-hour volume of $1.41 billion. $ETH is up a nearly identical 2.37%, but its 24-hour volume reads $475.34 million — roughly one-third of Bitcoin's. On the surface, the two assets are moving in lockstep. Under the surface, Ethereum is doing it on significantly lighter participation. That tells you something critical: ETH is not leading this move. It is being pulled along.

When an asset follows rather than leads, the follow-through becomes fragile. A market cap of $194.78 billion for ETH versus $1,205.25 billion for BTC (CoinMarketCap data) confirms the dominance gap has not closed. If you are allocating capital between these two right now, the relative risk profile matters more than the absolute percentage gain on any given day.

Now let us map the levels that matter, because this is where survival begins.

For $ETH, the 72-hour support sits at $1,550.20. If price holds above that zone, it tells you buyers are still defending the lower boundary of this consolidation. A bounce from there keeps the short-term structure intact and gives you a defined risk point — you know exactly where the thesis breaks. If ETH loses $1,550.20 on a closing basis, the range is broken to the downside, and the next support becomes an open question. That is the scenario where being patient costs nothing but being aggressive costs a lot.

On the upside, resistance at $1,646.26 is the ceiling. If ETH clears that level with volume — meaning volume materially above the current $475.34 million daily pace — it signals genuine demand stepping in, not just passive drift. A clean break above resistance shifts the structure from consolidation to potential trend continuation. Until that happens, approaching resistance is where experienced traders reduce exposure, not add to it. Tap $ETH to set your alerts around those levels right now.

For $BTC, the picture is similar but the stakes are larger. Support rests at $57,800.19 and resistance at $61,334.00. Bitcoin holding above $57,800.19 means the broader market structure remains constructive. Losing that level — especially on a day when an analyst is already warning about further downside after what has been called the worst June since 2022 — would likely drag the entire altcoin complex with it, ETH included. That is the systemic risk nobody wants to talk about at a +2% green candle. The level to watch is $61,334.00 on the topside; a rejection there after repeated attempts often precedes a sharper pullback. Tap $BTC to keep that chart front and center.

Here is how a risk-conscious trader frames exposure in this environment. ETH is range-bound with a slight upward bias but declining relative volume. The asymmetric play is not to predict the breakout — it is to define your maximum acceptable loss before the breakout happens. If you hold a position here, your stop belongs below $1,550.20, not at some round number you picked because it felt right. If you are flat and waiting, resistance at $1,646.26 is your decision point: a confirmed break with volume gives you a reason to engage; a rejection gives you a reason to stay patient.

The broader backdrop adds caution. Meanwhile, outlier movers like M (+56.9%) and RIF (+45.3%) on CoinMarketCap remind you that speculation is alive — but speculation and risk management are not the same discipline.

Initial jobless claims are expected to tick up slightly, which can only partially offset the downside on the employment side, but it cannot change the underlying hawkish logic driven by wages. title: BTC Rebounds From New Yearly Low While ETH and XRP Hold Key Support
subTitle:
Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), and XRP are showing signs of stabilizing after a sharp selloff. Bitcoin briefly dropped to a new yearly low of $57,800 on Wednesday before recovering toward $59,000. Meanwhile, Ethereum is holding above the crucial $1,500 support zone, while XRP continues to defend the psychological $1.00 level. Although the broader trend remains bearish, these price levels could determine whether a short-term recovery develops.

Bitcoin rebounds after touching a fresh yearly low
Bitcoin slipped to a new yearly low of $57,800 before bouncing back to around $59,000. Even with the recovery, the overall technical picture remains weak, as BTC continues to trade well below its major Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs). The 50-day EMA at $66,352, the 100-day EMA at $70,133, and the 200-day EMA at $76,276 all remain overhead, highlighting strong resistance and reinforcing the prevailing downtrend.
Momentum indicators also point to continued caution. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) sits near 32, suggesting bearish momentum is still in place despite the recent bounce. At the same time, the Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) has turned slightly negative around the zero line, indicating that buying momentum remains limited.
If buyers gain traction, Bitcoin's first hurdle lies near the $64,004 resistance level, followed by the 50-day EMA at $66,352. A stronger recovery could then target the 100-day EMA at $70,133 and the 200-day EMA at $76,276.
For sentiment to shift meaningfully, BTC would need to close above these major moving averages. Until then, failure to reclaim the $64,000 area could leave the cryptocurrency exposed to another decline toward the key psychological support at $55,000.
Ethereum defends the $1,500 support zone
Ethereum is trading around $1,586, remaining above the important $1,500 support level. Despite holding this area, the broader outlook remains negative, with ETH still trading below its 50-day, 100-day, and 200-day EMAs, which are positioned between roughly $1,815 and $2,286.
The RSI is hovering near 34, reflecting ongoing selling pressure, while the MACD has edged slightly higher, suggesting bearish momentum may be easing rather than signaling a confirmed trend reversal.
On the upside, the first major resistance comes at the 50-day EMA near $1,814. Above that, the 100-day EMA around $1,993 and the $2,000 horizontal resistance create a significant supply zone. The 200-day EMA near $2,285 remains the next major obstacle if the recovery strengthens.
Should selling pressure return, Ethereum's next key support sits near $1,385, where buyers may attempt to slow any further decline.
XRP holds above the psychological $1.00 level
XRP is trading around $1.047, continuing to hold above the important $1.00 psychological support. However, the short-term trend remains bearish, with the token trading below its 50-day EMA at $1.1937, 100-day EMA at $1.3019, and 200-day EMA at $1.5145.
Price also remains below the upper boundary of a descending parallel channel near $1.1600, indicating that sellers still have control. The RSI is holding near 34, while a flattening MACD histogram suggests downside momentum is beginning to stabilize, though there are no clear signs of a bullish reversal yet.
The first resistance is located around the channel's upper boundary near $1.1600, followed by the 50-day EMA at $1.1937. Beyond that, the $1.3000 resistance area aligns closely with the 100-day EMA, creating another significant barrier. A sustained rally would then face the 200-day EMA near $1.5145 before testing the major resistance around $1.9000.
With no strong support levels immediately below current prices, XRP needs a daily close above the $1.16 to $1.19 resistance zone to ease bearish pressure. Until that happens, the risk of another leg lower remains elevated.

title: One Candle From Liquidation: The High-Leverage Trap
subTitle:
Last week, a trader opened a 150x long on $ETH with a $2,500 target and watched the unrealized PnL explode past +6,300 USDT in hours.

That’s the kind of screenshot that triggers instant FOMO. Most people see the profit, not the liquidation risk sitting one candle away. In crypto, the hardest part isn’t spotting momentum. It’s knowing whether you’re catching the start of a real trend or becoming exit liquidity.

What makes this setup interesting is how familiar it feels. We saw the same psychology during previous $ETH rebounds after heavy sell-offs: traders pile into high leverage the moment sentiment flips bullish. Back in earlier recovery phases, aggressive longs worked fast when ETH reclaimed key levels, but overcrowded leverage also led to brutal wipeouts when momentum stalled.

This time, the market backdrop looks different from many short-lived pumps. $BTC holding strength while $ETH gains over 3% in a session suggests traders are rotating back into majors instead of chasing random hype. Still, 150x leverage turns even a 0.6% move against you into danger territory. The profit screenshot tells one story. The risk management behind it tells the real one.

Are we watching the start of another sustained $ETH comeback cycle, or just another leverage-fueled spike before volatility resets the board?

【The market is repeating the late-2018 script—but do you understand it?】

In December 2018, the market was in full lament: BTC fell to 3200, ETH dropped below $100, and the FNG index was also 19. Back then, everyone said it was over—zero it all, this time is different. So what happened next? V turned.

I’m not saying history will simply repeat, but the current situation really does feel uncomfortably familiar. FNG at 19, the weekly average only 14, yet ETH is quietly rebounding. +3.5% in 24 hours isn’t the main point—the key is that at this level, someone has started picking it up.

Let me share my recap.

First, the directional choice is getting close. Price has been stuck between 1533 and 1669 for a while. Over 7 days it’s down 1.1%, but trading volume has clearly expanded. This kind of move isn’t something retail traders can pull off—institutions are probing the direction. Next week, if there’s a breakout above 1669 with volume, the short-term bulls will be confirmed.

Second, a divergence signal has appeared. The FNG index is 19—extreme market panic—but ETH hasn’t made new lows. Historically, this kind of divergence often suggests that selling pressure has begun to exhaust. I’m not saying it will surge immediately, but the characteristics of a bottom area are becoming more obvious.

Third, valuation. Down 67% from the ATH. From a bubble perspective, it’s definitely oversold. But low valuation doesn’t automatically mean it will rise right away—you still need the fundamentals’ story to remain.

I admit I was wrong in my prediction last week. I thought it would break below 1533 to test even lower levels directly, but the bulls’ follow-through support has been stronger than expected. However, that’s not a bad thing—when you’re wrong, admit it, adjust your view, and keep watching.

Next week, I’ll focus on two things: whether trading volume can keep expanding, and whether 1669 can be broken through effectively. Don’t chase—wait for confirmation.

Here’s a real question for you: when the FNG index is 19, how many people around you are still talking about belief? And how many have already completely given up and stopped watching?

content:
【市场正在重复2018年底剧本，但你读懂了吗】

2018年12月，市场一片哀嚎，BTC跌到3200，ETH跌破100刀，FNG指数也是19。那时候所有人都说完了、归零了、这次不一样。然后呢？V转。

我不是在说历史会简单重复，但眼下这个局面确实眼熟得让人不适。FNG 19，周均才14，ETH却在悄悄反弹了。24小时+3.5%不是重点，重点是它在这个位置开始有人接了。

说说我的复盘。

第一，方向选择临近。价格卡在1533到1669之间已经有一阵子，7天还跌了1.1%，但成交量明显放大。这不是散户能搞出来的动静，机构在试探方向。下周如果带量突破1669，短期多头就确认了。

第二，背离信号出现。FNG指数19，市场极度恐慌，但ETH没有创新低。这种背离历史上往往意味着抛压衰竭。不是说马上涨，但底部区域特征越来越明显。

第三，估值问题。较ATH跌了67%，从泡沫角度看确实超跌。但估值低不代表马上涨，还得看基本面的故事还在不在。

我承认上周预判有失误。以为会直接破1533测试更低位置，结果多头的承接比预期强。不过这不是坏事，错了就认，调整观点继续看。

下周盯两件事：成交量能不能持续放大，1669能不能有效突破。别追高，等确认。

问你们一个现实问题：当FNG指数19的时候，你身边有多少人还在谈信仰？又有多少人已经彻底躺平不看了？

title: Ethereum Records Its Worst Streak Ever. Three Consecutive Losing Quarters Raise Investor Concerns
subTitle:
Ethereum has entered uncharted territory. The world's second-largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization has now closed three consecutive quarters in negative territory for the first time in its history, marking an unprecedented bearish milestone. ETH is currently trading around $1,560, representing roughly a 70% decline from its all-time high.
Despite the prolonged downturn, analysts remain divided. While some warn that further downside is still possible, others believe Ethereum is approaching a zone where long-term investors may begin accumulating once again.

A Historic Milestone Investors Would Rather Forget
Ethereum finished the second quarter in the red, extending its losing streak to three consecutive negative quarters—a first since the asset was launched.
Since reaching an all-time high near $5,000 in 2025, ETH has steadily declined by approximately 70%. The prolonged weakness has been driven by a combination of unfavorable macroeconomic conditions, weaker investor sentiment, and continued capital outflows from risk assets.
Seasonality also presents another challenge. Historical data shows that July has ended negatively in six of the past ten years, suggesting elevated volatility could persist throughout the coming weeks.

$1,700 Remains the Level Bulls Must Reclaim
Technical analysts continue to focus on $1,700, which has emerged as Ethereum's most important resistance level.
Crypto analyst Ted notes that Ethereum has recently shown greater resilience than Bitcoin. However, he cautions that the asset remains in a vulnerable position.
According to Ted, reclaiming $1,700 would significantly improve Ethereum's technical outlook. Failure to break above this level, however, would increase the probability of another move toward fresh local lows.

Some Analysts Believe the Bottom Is Near
Not everyone expects another major collapse.
Analyst Crypto with Haris argues that predictions calling for Ethereum to fall toward $1,000 are overly pessimistic.
He believes Ethereum has already absorbed much of the bearish pressure and is now building a strong demand zone between $1,500 and $1,600.
Even if Bitcoin experiences another correction, Haris considers the $1,200–$1,300 range to be a far more realistic downside target for ETH during the current market cycle.

Whale Selling Continues to Pressure the Market
On-chain data also supports the cautious outlook.
Crypto analyst Ali Martinez reported that Ethereum whales sold nearly $900 million worth of ETH within a single week. Such large-scale selling activity typically increases downward pressure and makes sustained recoveries more difficult.
Meanwhile, blockchain analytics platform Lookonchain revealed that one investor recently sold nearly 2,500 ETH, realizing a loss of more than $4.3 million.

What Comes Next for Ethereum?
In the coming weeks, investors will closely monitor macroeconomic developments alongside activity in the derivatives market. One of the most important upcoming events will be the monthly options expiration, which has historically been associated with increased volatility.
Ethereum is now approaching a critical stage. If buyers manage to reclaim the $1,700 level, market sentiment could gradually improve. However, if selling pressure persists and large investors continue reducing their positions, the second-largest cryptocurrency may face another test of its key support zones before a sustainable recovery begins.

title: BTC Nears $61,334 Resistance as Funding Flows Signal a Critical Decision Point
subTitle:
Bitcoin is pressing against its 72-hour resistance at $61,334, currently trading at $60,838.87 on Binance with a 2.83% gain over the last 24 hours. Ethereum mirrors that momentum at $1,631.29, up 2.46%, sitting just below its own 72-hour ceiling of $1,646.26. Both assets are coiling at the top of their recent ranges, and what happens next is less about headlines and more about the derivatives plumbing underneath.

Funding rates are the mechanism most retail traders overlook, but they are the clearest real-time gauge of whether the market is overleveraged in one direction. When perpetual futures trade at a premium to spot, longs pay shorts a periodic fee — that is positive funding. When the premium flips negative, shorts pay longs. The rate itself is a crowdsourced signal: high positive funding means the crowd is aggressively long, which historically makes the market vulnerable to sharp liquidations if price stalls. Slightly positive or neutral funding, by contrast, often precedes healthier trend continuation because the move is not built on borrowed conviction.

Right now both $BTC and $ETH are testing the upper boundary of a defined range without the kind of extreme funding spikes that marked previous local tops. That is a structural detail worth understanding. It suggests that the 2.83% and 2.46% daily moves are being driven more by spot demand and moderate leveraged positioning than by the frothy, one-sided crowded trades that tend to reverse violently. In plain terms: the rally has room to breathe, but it still needs to prove it can convert resistance into support.

Here is the map that matters for $BTC this week. Support sits at $57,800.19 — that is the floor buyers have defended over the past 72 hours. If price holds above that level on any pullback, the dip-buy thesis remains intact and the market structure stays bullish. Resistance is $61,334.00, and Bitcoin is trading within 1% of it right now. A clean break and hold above $61,334 on convincing volume would flip that level into a new support zone and open the path toward retesting higher supply areas. If $BTC gets rejected here and slides back below $57,800, that would signal sellers have reclaimed control and the range-bound chop continues — or worse, accelerates to the downside. That second scenario is exactly what one analyst flagged when warning that BTC could drop further after its worst June since 2022.

Ethereum tells a parallel story with tighter numbers. The 72-hour support is $1,550.20, and resistance is $1,646.26. ETH is trading at $1,631.29, meaning it has roughly $15 of air before it tags that resistance ceiling. If $ETH can punch through $1,646 and consolidate above it, that is the signal that capital is rotating back into risk-on altcoin exposure. If it fails and loses $1,550 on the downside, the bearish case strengthens and funding will likely flip negative as leveraged longs capitulate.

One more thing the derivatives market is telling us: the notable movers today — M up 76.5%, RIF up 56.7%, DEEP up 18.5% according to CoinMarketCap — are happening while headline risk is elevated. France is cracking down after a wave of 77 crypto-related physical attacks, and Venice AI just became a unicorn with a $65 million Series A. The combination of institutional capital flowing into crypto-adjacent infrastructure and violent real-world crime against holders is a tension the derivatives market prices in through volatility premiums. When implied volatility rises but funding stays neutral, it means traders expect a big move but are not yet betting on direction. That is precisely the setup where a breakout above resistance or a breakdown below support triggers the most aggressive follow-through because positioning is balanced.

So the question is straightforward: will $BTC and $ETH convert these resistance levels into launchpads, or will the market hand control back to sellers at the ceiling? Watch the funding rate on your perpetual pairs alongside the price levels above. If funding creeps higher while price stalls at resistance, caution is warranted. If price breaks out and funding remains modest, the move has structural integrity.

What is your read — breakout or rejection? Drop your take below.

Not financial advice. Follow the builders.

Sui announced that the mainnet upgrade to the new version has been completed, with the protocol synchronized to version 128. The重点 is on improving developer testing efficiency and network runtime stability. The Solana Foundation has launched an on-chain governance framework aimed at validators, allowing major network issues to be handled through weighted voting. Final approval also requires a relatively high approval threshold. This initiative is expected to provide a clearer governance pathway for network upgrades and infrastructure adjustments, further reflecting Solana’s continued progress in institutionalized governance.

title: BlackRock moves $600M as Bitcoin momentum stalls
subTitle:
BlackRock just moved over $600M worth of $BTC and $ETH to prime brokerage wallets in 48 hours, and it happened right as Bitcoin started losing momentum.

Most retail traders get blindsided in moments like this. Price looks stable, everyone assumes the big money is holding, and then sudden liquidity hits the market and people end up panic selling the bottom.

On-chain flows like this matter because institutions rarely move coins without a reason. When large holders shift hundreds of millions in $BTC or $ETH to trading venues or broker custody, it often means one of two things: preparing to sell, or preparing to hedge. Either way, it increases short-term supply pressure right when the market is fragile.

The timing is the uncomfortable part. Bitcoin is already struggling to hold key levels, and big transfers during weak price action can amplify volatility. If even long-term allocators start rotating risk, smaller traders who bought the recent range tend to get squeezed first while liquidity gets tested.

Watching flows like this alongside market structure and assets like $BNB can reveal when “patient capital” might actually be repositioning instead of simply holding.

Do you see this as normal portfolio management, or the early signal of bigger distribution?
